author: opt-W1b

contract.sync_assumed: none beyond convergence of the logical warp
contract.k_range: [1, N] with MaxK = max(LW, next_pow2(k)) dividing N, k 8 to 64 measured
contract.n_range: N = LW x IPT, N over MaxK a power of two for the level-parallel loop, bf16 N <= 65536 (16-bit index), measured 32 to 256 at LW 32
contract.type_constraints: fp32 keys compared with fmaxf and fminf, bf16 keys with __hmax and __hmin, int32 index carried as the value and moved when the key moved
contract.nan_behavior: fmaxf, fminf, __hmax and __hmin return the non-NaN operand, so a NaN key loses every exchange and is never selected, never produced by focus-set inputs. -0.0 and +0.0 compare equal and keep their index
contract.tie_break_support: not supported: equal keys keep their network position (not_guaranteed only), see W1_eager_same for the index-in-key route
contract.sorted_output_support: inherent: the first k striped positions are sorted

correctness_notes: Oracle battery passed on every cell for variant and control, not_guaranteed only (ties keep their network position). W1 was run by two optimizer instances after a duplicate launch: opt-W1 (worktree cccl-topk-swarm-W1, variants W1_packed, W1_level, W1_reference_sub) and opt-W1b (this card, worktree cccl-topk-swarm-W1b, variants W1_eager_same, W1_level_same, W1_minmax_pairs, W1_level_pairs, W1_baseline, W1_kvcmp and their _sub forms). opt-W1b owns the N2 kill experiment on identical network code, the fp32 native min max pairs route and the sub-warp grid.

low_level: Same instruction mix as the eager pairs loop: fp32 N 128 k 32 latency kernel 1168 SASS instructions against 1136, 300 SHFL (key and index per stage), 306 FMNMX, 156 FSETP, 152 SEL in both. The level-parallel form keeps every tile's key and index live through the interleaved sorts and costs registers: 67 against 35 (bf16 N 128), 76 against 42 (bf16 N 256), 51 against 39 (fp32 N 128), 64 against 48 (fp32 N 256), no spills.

The register growth costs occupancy in the throughput regime: 5 or 6 blocks per SM against 6 for the eager pairs loop, so the throughput is equal or lower (bf16 N 256 k 32 119.4 against 125.1 Gelem/s, fp32 N 128 k 32 169.8 against 182.8) while the latency is better.
algorithmic: Kill cell N 64 k 32 (pairs): 1420 against 1369 cycles bf16 (0.96x), 753 against 720 fp32 (0.96x), the level-parallel form is slower where the two loops are the same DAG. From N 128 on the pairs network has twice the shuffle traffic of the packed one and the level structure starts to pay in latency: N 128 k 32 bf16 2673 against 3219 (1.20x), fp32 1754 against 2004 (1.14x), N 256 k 32 bf16 5943 against 6531 (1.10x), fp32 3739 against 4545 (1.22x), N 256 k 64 bf16 6596 against 7422 (1.13x), fp32 4153 against 4547 (1.09x), N 128 k 64 within 1 percent.

So the restructuring gains 10 to 22 percent in latency where the eager loop is shuffle-issue bound (two shuffles per stage, 4 or more tiles) and nothing where it is latency bound (one word per stage, or two tiles). It is a latency-only lever and it pays with registers, which the throughput regime takes back.
negative: At the kill cell the verdict is the same as on packed words: no gain, 0.96x. The 1.3x threshold of the N2 card is not reached anywhere, the best cell is 1.22x (fp32 N 256 k 32) with 16 more registers and lower throughput.
surprises: The eager pairs control itself is unstable across k at fixed MaxK: fp32 N 128 at k 8 and 16 measures 1649 cycles and at k 32 2004 cycles with the same network (1120 against 1136 SASS instructions, identical opcode histogram), the only source change being the predicate on the index store. The level-parallel form at k 32 (1754) is therefore partly a reschedule of the same work, see the W1_minmax_pairs card.
open_questions: Whether a level-parallel loop that releases the consumed tiles earlier (pairing adjacent registers so the compiler can retire them) keeps the latency gain without the register growth.
